articles.title: Emmy Rossum on Producing and Starring in 'Furious': "I Have Been 'Matrix'-Style Dodging Mega-Predators Since I Was Seven"
articles.summary: In front of an audience at the Newport Beach Film Festival, the actress reflects on her breakthrough in 'The Phantom of the Opera,' her quest for equal pay on 'Shameless' and her production company: "I like characters that are living in moral gray areas. That's something that I wasn't really able to do in the ingenue years."
articles.content:
"I have been Matrix -style dodging mega-predators since I was seven years old," actress-producer Emmy Rossum said during a recording of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast at the recent Newport Beach Film Festival , where she was being honored with the fest's Outstanding Performance in Television Award for her work on Hulu's Furious . The drama series, which she also produced, tells a cat-and-mouse tale of a female FBI agent (Rossum) and a young female serial killer (Lola Petticrew), both PTSD-afflicted survivors of sexual abuse. "So," Rossum continued, "I firsthand understand the nuance and complexity of being a young person in situations like this and of being a powerful professional woman in situations like this." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Awards Chatter' Podcast Jessica Lange on Bringing 'Long Day's Journey Into Night' Back to the Big Screen, Returning to 'American Horror Story' and Retirement Rumors News Emmy Rossum Named RAINN Ambassador Amid New Partnership to Deepen Public Understanding of Sexual Violence and Survivorship (Exclusive)

Rossum, who was once described by the late Roger Ebert as “a phenomenal talent,” is only 40, but she has been doing outstanding work for nearly 30 years — in films like 2000s Songcatcher , 2003's Mystic River , 2004's The Phantom of the Opera and 2013's Beautiful Creatures ; TV limited series such as Angelyne (2022) and The Crowded Room (2023); and, of course, for 110 episodes over nine seasons on the TV series Shameless (2011-2019), several episodes of which she also directed.

As Rossum's time on Shameless came to an end, she launched a production company, Composition 8, which she now runs with her husband, Mr. Robot creator Sam Esmail, and a development executive, Sara Moskowitz. Their first project was Angelyne , in which Rossum played the eponymous Los Angeles billboard queen. They have since made several others. Rossum explains, "The throughline in things that I've been looking for is: I like characters that are living in moral gray areas. That's something that I wasn't really able to do in the ingenue years." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But obtaining choice material is not easy for a small company, even one run by a top young actress. "We have to be scrappy because we're not LuckyChap [Margot Robbie's company], and we're not Hello Sunshine [Reese Witherspoon's company]," she explains. "We're three people with this mandate of wanting to tell complicated stories about women that talk about something in the zeitgeist and culture and where we are now — and make really entertaining and fun stuff."

What led them to Furious , their most successful project yet? Rossum recounts, "I was like, 'OK, well, we're not going to land any of the hot books, so where do we go look? We have to look where other people are not looking. Let's look at all of the old movies that nobody's looking at. Like, they were good, so why aren't we looking there? There's got to be one that's got a good skeleton that we can uncover and figure it out.'"

That led them to Bob Rafelson's 1987 cult classic Black Widow , which starred Debra Winger and Theresa Russell as an FBI agent and serial killer, respectively. The material was nearly 40 years old, but still "feels kind of contemporary," she felt, noting eerie parallels with everything from the Jeffrey Epstein saga to the "Jane Doe" case at Cornell. So Composition 8 obtained the rights and set about putting it together. Rossum sold the show to Hulu via a text, recruited Liz Meriwether ( The Dropout ) to serve as showrunner and set about preparing to play cop-turned-FBI agent Alice Black, meeting with and shadowing law enforcement officials, consulting psychotherapists, adding considerable muscle to her small physique and more. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She reflects, "It's interesting to play a character who can hold so many complexities, who can be infinitely, bottomlessly vulnerable and terrified and afraid to be weak at the same time as being incredibly manipulative and physically and emotionally powerful and dogged and smart and underestimated. It was the role that haunted me the most, and it was a benefit that I came on so early, because I felt that I was working on the character for three years before we started shooting."

The first season of Furious , which rolled out in July and August, was described by The New York Times as “remarkable.” Rossum's part, meanwhile, was described by The Guardian as “the role of her life.” For it, she is now in serious contention for end-of-the-year honors — best actress in a drama series Critics Choice, Golden Globe and Actor Awards — and, next year, she might well become the first person with the name Emmy to, well, win one.

In the meantime, though, she's headed back to work: a second season of Furious was ordered just before its season one finale aired , and it starts shooting in January. She can't wait — but she also wants the industry to know that she's not only interested in acting in stuff that she also produces: "I'm still in the incoming-call business, so please hire me! I want great roles."

articles.title: 'Home Alone' Sequel in Development at Disney With Macaulay Culkin, Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg
articles.summary: Culkin is expected to reprise his role as Kevin McCallister, while Rogen and Goldberg are writing and producing the sequel.
articles.content:
The Home Alone franchise is expanding. A sequel to the beloved holiday classic is in early development at Disney , The Hollywood Reporter has confirmed.

Macaulay Culkin , who portrayed Kevin McCallister in the original 1990 film and its 1992 sequel, Home Alone 2: Lost in New York , is expected to reprise his role. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg , the longtime comedy duo behind Superbad , Pineapple Express , Neighbors , Sausage Party and The Studio , are writing and producing the film under their Point Grey banner. The duo is also working with Culkin on his idea for the sequel. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Disney and AWS Team Up to Create AI-Powered 'Star Wars' Robots Business Disney Beats Wall Street Expectations as Entertainment and Parks Power Latest Quarter

Chris Columbus directed the first two films , which grossed a combined $836.3 million worldwide. No director is attached at this early stage to the new installment.

The news comes after Culkin expressed interest in revisiting the character in recent years. During a stop on his A Nostalgic Night with Macaulay Culkin tour in November 2025, the actor said he "wouldn't be completely allergic" to returning as Kevin, provided the project was right. He also shared his idea for a potential sequel, which would see Kevin as a widowed or divorced father raising a child of his own. In his proposed story, Kevin would find himself locked out of his house, with his son setting traps to keep him out — reversing the original film's premise.

According to reports, Culkin later met with Disney Motion Pictures chief David Greenbaum over the summer to pitch his idea for a sequel.

President Trump suggested on Friday that the bill to create a federal tax credit for film and TV production may also include support for theaters.

Taking questions at the White House, Trump was asked about areas of cooperation with the incoming Democratic majority in Congress. After praising the Democratic leaders and briefly touching on healthcare, he pivoted to support for U.S. movies and TV shows. "We're working on a bill for entertainment, which is motion picture, television — we're thinking about adding certain other elements, like for instance theaters," Trump said. But we're actively in negotiations on that, and that's going to be very bipartisan." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Trump has previously endorsed a production incentive, which would provide producers with a 20%-30% credit on domestic labor costs. The reference to theaters was new, however.

Cinema United, the trade group representing the theater industry, has been pushing for a bill to subsidize renovation of theaters. The SCREEN Act , introduced in July, would create a 30% tax credit, with a maximum award ranging from $250,000 to $500,000 per site.

Michael O'Leary, the president and CEO of Cinema United, hailed the bill upon its introduction, saying that towns across the country "will see a tangible and positive cultural and economic impact in their local communities."

A year after revealing a Miss Piggy movie in the works, Jennifer Lawrence has shared an update on the Muppet solo outing.

The Oscar-winning actress, who is developing the project with fellow producer Emma Stone and screenwriter Cole Escola , teased the status of the script in response to a fan question on Watch What Happens Live .

"I don't know! I always get in trouble for saying stuff," said Lawrence, before reluctantly sharing: "Um, we have a first draft!"

articles.title: Channing Tatum's Josephine Is Not An Easy Watch, But Here's Why I Think It's A Must-See Film
articles.summary: It's a movie that will always haunt me.
articles.content:
I was fortunate enough to see Josephine at the 62nd Chicago International Film Festival, and it’s quickly becoming one of my favorite films of the year. The film explores collective trauma, female rage, the justice system, and so much more.

Josephine works best with minimal knowledge of the plot. Therefore, I will try not to spoil any major storylines. At its core, the film portrays society and how it often scars and fails women and girls.

Many films touch upon difficult subjects. However, not many of them create an atmosphere as well as Josephine . You feel the weight of everything. The subject matter has been done a lot, and sometimes in ways that sensationalize an event to the point of losing the horror in it. Josephine treats the subject matter with care. We need films like this, especially given some of the recent headlines.

Many of the best courtroom dramas often end with a sense of justice being served. Whether Josephine ends with a positive result or a negative result, it doesn’t matter. It ends with a sense that nothing is completely resolved. That feels more realistic than movies with an impressive lawyer who saves the day.

articles.title: 'Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow' Review: Oobah Butler Exposes Modern Life's Many Frauds in Nathan Fielder-esque HBO Comedy Doc
articles.summary: The British journalist/prankster explores the scams behind wine, music, dating apps, wellness products and more in this five-episode series.
articles.content:
With You Can See Everything putting Nathan Fielder on the minds of viewers who had never heard of Nathan for You or The Rehearsal , it's likely that HBO announced and scheduled new docu-comedy Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow in the hopes that people would compare series host/creator Oobah Butler to presumptive awards darling Fielder.

It's a borderline impossible comparison to avoid, particularly in the United States given that Butler's profile is far lower here than in the UK, where he likely finds it harder to perpetuate his brand of fact-based pranking on an unsuspecting audience. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business 'GTA VI' Generates $3.79 Billion in "Day One" Sales Movies Teyana Taylor Sells Female-Driven Comedy to Warner Bros. (Exclusive) Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow The Bottom Line Entertaining, but too rushed to be deep or humane. Airdate: 11 p.m. Sunday, November 22 (HBO) Creator/Star: Oobah Butler Director: Daniel Lucchesi

I don't think that tying Butler and Fielder together quite captures the full Oobah Butler experience. His cheeky brand of muckraking, honed over years adjacent to actual journalism, has at least as much in common with Louis Theroux, Michael Moore or Mads Brügger, among other puckish truth-tellers. This doesn't mean that Butler does what he does better than Fielder does what he does, either — just that it isn't a guarantee that if you like one that you'll like the other, or if you hate one that you'll hate the other. Compatible! But different.

Even though it's airing on Sunday nights at 11, Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow fits solidly into HBO's vaunted Friday late-night slot that The Rehearsa l and How To with John Wilson and Neighbors have filled with reality-based pseudo-mirth in the past. It's frequently eye-opening and occasionally funny, and it captures some important truths about the modern condition without ever feeling as revelatory or profound as it obviously thinks itself to be. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Butler, who has pursued his interest in scams and socially endorsed frauds through Vice exposés, a bestselling book and a variety of television documentaries, is (or was, given that some of these scams date back to COVID times) based in New York, where he can apparently fool people in various ambitious ways.

If you recall how Butler gamed the system back in 2017 to transform his garden shed into London's top-rated restaurant on TripAdvisor, you're prepared for the gambits that play out over the five episodes of Scams for a Better Tomorrow .

Each episode is a too-tightly-contained attempt at a comparable prank, starting with "Wellness," in which he attempts to create, market and sell a nonexistent product called "Lacrimé," a serum derived from the tears of children. In "Wine," he attempts to turn garbage wine from spoiled, smoky Napa Valley grapes into a commercial success. In "Dating Apps," he attempts to create, well, a dating app driven by AI. In "Music," he attempts to transform a 15-second musical hook into a viral social media phenomenon and then into a charting hit song. And, finally, in "Royalty," he attempts to discover what it would be like to be a royal by, well, becoming a royal.

I say "attempting," but at least to varying degrees, he succeeds in these missions, with the entertainment not so much coming from the thing he's doing as the way he's doing it.

Some of the facets of his scams — or counter-scams, I suppose — are predictable and surface-level. Like who ever would have guessed that if you get your friends and loved ones to spend a buck purchasing your dismal musical effort that you can make your way onto a fringe iTunes chart? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In other cases, Butler's strategies are far more nefarious and amusing, achieving their goals in unexpected or vaguely disturbing ways. He learns the workarounds and loopholes of wellness product claims and endorsements, attempts psychological manipulation to allow his subpar wine to win competitions, and even seeks out single princesses online looking for a potential mate.

And sometimes, there's a truly devious architecture to his process, like the way he gets a group of singles on his fake AI dating site to text each other while believing they're texting with a digital character.

The elaborately constructed pranks are the ones that feel the most like what Fielder did for several years on Nathan for You , the key difference being that despite his aura of detachment, Fielder cares about the people he's tricking. "Caring" can take the form of either contempt or actual empathy, which causes the viewer to either root for or against the people he's interacting with. That you can't guarantee from episode to episode whether, and how, you want Fielder to succeed becomes the uncomfortable friction of that series. The Rehearsal is much more dedicated to Fielder's subterfuge as an orchestrated operation, but it's the human touch that allows for emotional resonance.

Butler is, at least in the case of this series, not especially interested in "people." He's interested in the industries and institutions that we naïvely trust and all the ways their bugs can be exploited and manipulated. He wants us to understand that the wellness industry is a scam, that royalty is a scam, that contemporary, social media-driven music is a scam. If he has to run over ordinary and extraordinary people to make this point, whether it's the wine critic from The New York Times , the princess of Cambodia or those duped daters, he struggles to make us believe that he cares. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Perhaps to combat the notion that he's only invested in the process, to prove that he has a soul and an investment in the human side of his endeavor, Butler has several episodes built around conversations with attorneys, to whom he's explaining the full game. He talks the attorneys through what he's done with overt and unconvincing displays of concern, asking repeatedly if he's broken any laws and looking for reassurance that he isn't the villain here.

These conversations ultimately are there to answer the question of "How does he get away with this?" rather than "How does he sleep at night?" but Butler sometimes puts on a sad affect as if he has regrets.

Those alleged regrets get lost in a hurry, because at 30 minutes apiece, Scams for a Better Tomorrow simply doesn't have time. Even Oobah, who sometimes resembles a Chris Lilley sketch character minus the tendency toward blackface (or a John Early gag), is presented as the man pushing everything forward, not the hero or villain of the story. He's busy and the show is busy and episodes are often too rushed to be satisfying.

In this respect, Scams for a Better Tomorrow works almost in contrast to The Rehearsal , where Fielder's ability to build a bar set on a soundstage or mount a reality singing competition or tell Sully's life story with puppets is meant to appear almost magical in its sleight of hand. Butler is constantly showing his receipts by the handful. articles.title: Selena Gomez’s Reaction To Martin Short Accidentally Cutting Her Wedding Cake Is As Funny As I’d Hoped

articles.content:
It's been well established that Selena Gomez , Martin Short and Steve Martin know how to get into hilarious trouble on Only Murders in the Building , which you can stream with a Hulu subscription . However, the members of the unexpected trio know how to do that in real life too. Need an example? Look no further than the time Martin Short accidentally cut Gomez's wedding cake , and her hilarious reaction to it.

I do love that Short tried his hardest to cover it up, but I can’t say I blame him for cutting into the cake. He revealed that there were different sections at the reception with couches and groups of people, and he simply thought there was a cake in each section.

Considering how close Gomez and Short have become over the years, I love that there were no hard feelings over the accidental cake cutting. It also further proves why they’re bestie goals . Even now, she laughed the entire time retelling the story, which Short says he is “blameless” in.

The friendship between Short, Martin, and Gomez is definitely the best thing to come out of Only Murders in the Building . Of course, Short and Martin have long been friends, but I definitely feel like Gomez was the missing piece. Now, I hope there are many more funny stories like this to come.

In an unprecedented move Laika is giving back to the Portland Oregon community where the film not only was made, but also is set.

This Thanksgiving weekend , specifically on November 29, the studio will open the doors and invite local audiences to complimentary screenings all across town. So far 15 theatres adding up to 7900 seats and 37+ showings have already signed on and that number is expected to grow substantially. The idea to do this citywide free event actually came from its legendary six time-Oscar nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel who spent a good deal of time in Portland making the stop motion epic directed by Travis Knight who is also CEO of Laika. Portland has been one of the top grossing markets for the film - seven of the top ten markets are in the city - but rather than continuing to make residents pay to see their moment of cinema glory, Laika is offering the chance for everyone to see it for free. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A free Nintendo Switch Online promotion has been announced by Nintendo, letting Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 users snag three months of Nintendo Switch Online for free. Nintendo Switch Online at the monthly rate costs $4 a month, so this represents a savings of $12. This may not seem like much money, but right now, just on the Nintendo eShop, $12 gets you games like Slay the Spire , Persona 4 Golden , and LEGO Harry Potter Collection. Further, in an economy where a simple candy bar costs over $2, any bit of money that can be saved quickly adds up.

In addition to some Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake freebies , Nintendo Switch Online subscribers on both Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 have until December 6th to get a 3-month free extension to their Nintendo Switch Online subscription when they purchase 12 months of a subscription. This 12 month subscription can be a brand new subscription as well as an extension to a pre-exisiting subscription itself.

Right now, the offer is limited to the UK . Whether it will come to the United States and other markets remains to be seen, but there's a decent chance it will. If not, there are ways to take advantage of the deal without actually being in the UK. Meanwhile, this offer is not only available with the standard tier, but the Expansion Pack tier as well. The Expansion Pack is not available monthly. It can only be purchased at the 12-month rate, which costs $50. Effectively it's a similar amount of savings compared to three months of the monthly subscription to the standard tier, which is marked up in price because it's not 12 months bundeled.

It's quite rare for Nintendo to runs promotions on Nintendo Switch Online, even during the holiday season. Nintendo Switch Online is already very cheap compared to PlayStation Plus and Xbox Game Pass, so there likely isn't much wiggle room to run these type of promotions. Whatever the reason why, the point is these type of NSO promotions don't happen very often, so those who can should take advantage of this one while it's live and an option.

Nintendo Switch Online is available via Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. Right now, there is no official word or rumblings of any major changes coming to the subscription service, such as a price increase, but it does look like a new console platform may be coming to NSO soon .

articles.title: I Need To Point Out One Unexpected (And Positive) Side Effect Of That Kelly Clarkson Bird Brouhaha
articles.summary: At least some good came out of all this.
articles.content:
Kelly Clarkson 's feud with the Art of Play store became one of the strangest stories of 2026, as who would've thought a story about a pop star trying to buy an animatronic bird would draw so much attention? While the beloved Clarkson might've taken some hits in the court of public opinion , it sounds like the artist on the other side of the drama saw a big boost in patronage.

The 70-year-old artist who lives in Seattle isn't trying to ramp up the amount he's doing these days, but he is grateful for the spotlight on the work he's made throughout his life. Out of all the hatred that came from this drama, I'm happy to hear some positivity came out of it, too.

For those needing a refresher, this all started when Kelly Clarkson wandered into a Brooklyn store and inquired about the price of an animatronic bird on the wall. There's a discrepancy about what happened afterward, but the pop star went online and alleged that a worker at the store implied she couldn't afford the asking price, apparently not knowing who she was.

articles.summary: Although Solo Leveling has remained quiet for a while, with no official release dates announced for any of its projects, the franchise's live-action series has just taken a promising step closer to release. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although Solo Leveling has remained quiet for a while, with no official release dates announced for any of its projects, the franchise's live-action series has just taken a promising step closer to release. Netflix's live-action adaptation was first announced in July 2025, featuring a promising cast and the surprising decision to follow the K-Drama format. Filming for the series, however, began in May this year, and so far, there have been two updates from the leading actors offering insight into how production is unfolding. It is safe to say that the project is aiming for an ambitious release and could become a live-action adaptation that fans will remember.

However, no release date or window has been officially announced as of this writing. A report from Financial News , however, may have just confirmed a 2028 release window for the series. South Korean entertainment and production company CJ ENM recently celebrated the 10th anniversary of one of its programs, O'PEN, which supports aspiring screenwriters, songwriters, and, more recently, novelists. The announcement emerged from one of the program's writers, who is speculated to also be involved in writing Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action K-Drama. A closer look at the details makes the potential 2028 release window for this project all the more plausible.

Considering that filming for the live-action adaptation only began in May this year, and the latest update from actress Han So-hee, who plays Cha Hae-in , suggests that filming is still underway, there is still some time before production comes to an end. It is evident that a significant amount of effort will go into post-production to bring the series' fantastical elements to life. This will require the production company to dedicate a considerable amount of time, especially considering that the first season will consist of seven episodes. Since it is also following the K-Drama format, fans can expect longer episodes, with the first season potentially covering a major portion of the story, perhaps reaching the point covered by the anime's first two seasons.

This gives the anonymous report from Financial News much more credibility. With this, Solo Leveling has finally secured a potential release window for a visual project for the first time since the anime concluded in 2025. There is no doubt that the most ambitious upcoming project is the anime movie, Solo Leveling: Beyond the System , which will immediately follow the anime and precede its third season. However, there is still no confirmed release date for the movie, despite fans speculating that it could arrive next year.

That said, there is still a possibility that the anime movie could be the next project fans get to see, potentially arriving in late 2027 or early 2028. Either way, these promising updates suggest that after two years of silence in the visual and audio formats, the Solo Leveling franchise is preparing for major releases over the next couple of years, once again capturing the industry's attention and potentially breaking even more records upon its return.
